facts.text: Grannis was incorporated in October 1899 and began as a railroad depot that grew alongside the timber industry.
Over the years, Grannis expanded its economy to include fruit and poultry production, reflecting its agricultural heritage.
Today, Grannis still carries a strong sense of history and community pride, making it a welcoming home for its residents.
Grannis sits in southwestern Arkansas, within Polk County, and its rural character combined with an accessible location makes it inviting to live, work, and visit.
Grannis lies at latitude 34°14′20″N and longitude 94°19′42″W, placing it in the heart of southwestern Arkansas.
In the 1950s, Grannis was assigned to Gillham schools in Sevier County, reflecting the region’s shifting educational boundaries.
